about: Hand-fixed part breakdowns. tools/build_data.py uses these instead of its own split. Each part is [glyph, position], or [glyph, position, [KanjiVG stroke numbers]] when the glyph needs a drawing; glyphs must be palette tiles or their forms (data/parts.json), positions one of left, right, top, bottom, outer, inner, whole, none. Say why, so the next person knows what KanjiVG got wrong.

万.why: The two strokes under the line draw 力; KanjiVG leaves them loose.

三.why: Three loose strokes otherwise; 二 is a tile.

円.why: The stroke and line sit inside 冂; KanjiVG gives no positions, so they came out none.

年.why: KanjiVG splits 干 around the other strokes, which left loose strokes and an enclosure.

実.why: The bottom is 夫 under one more line; KanjiVG leaves the lines loose.

寒.why: The middle is 共 with an extra line; KanjiVG has it as loose strokes and a split 三.

声.why: KanjiVG leaves the bottom as four loose strokes; it reads as 尸 with a stroke down its left.

勤.why: KanjiVG's 菫 isn't a tile and its bottom is loose strokes; it draws 口 over 王.

無.why: KanjiVG leaves the top as eight loose strokes. 卌 isn't in JIS, so its strokes are listed for the drawing.

舞.why: Same top as 無, which KanjiVG leaves as loose strokes.
